seoTitle: Free Content Calendar Generator in Markdown or CSV
metaDescription: Assign a list of topics to dates on a daily, weekday, weekly, biweekly or monthly cadence and export as Markdown or CSV. Free, in your browser.
intro: Enter your topics, a start date and a cadence, and get a dated content calendar as a Markdown table or CSV, ready to paste into a doc or spreadsheet.
why:
A list of article ideas is not a plan until each one has a date. Laying them out by hand in a spreadsheet is tedious, and it gets worse when you want weekdays only, or a monthly slot that must handle short months.

This generator takes your topics in order and assigns each a date from your start date at the cadence you choose: every day, weekdays only, weekly, every two weeks or monthly. The output has date, weekday, topic, channel and a Planned status, in Markdown for wikis and pull requests, or CSV for spreadsheets. The dates come from simple calendar rules, and nothing is stored or uploaded.
howTo: Enter your topics, one per line, in the order you want to publish them.
Set the start date as YYYY-MM-DD, the cadence and the channel name.
Choose the output format: markdown or csv.
Copy the calendar into your document, board or spreadsheet.

faq.q: How does the monthly cadence handle short months?
faq.a: It keeps the same day of the month where possible. If the start date is the 31st, shorter months use their last day, such as 28 or 30 February.

faq.q: What does the weekdays cadence do?
faq.a: It schedules one topic per working day, skipping Saturdays and Sundays. If your start date falls on a weekend, the first topic moves to the following Monday.

faq.q: Does it know about public holidays?
faq.a: No. It only skips weekends, and only in weekdays mode. Adjust dates by hand around holidays that matter to your audience.

faq.q: Why is the date format YYYY-MM-DD?
faq.a: It is unambiguous, sorts correctly and imports cleanly into spreadsheets. A start date in another format is rejected with a message asking for an example like 2026-01-05.
